summary: Owner-approved closure with bounded provider-infrastructure deviation. Five deterministic public-MCP loadouts (Guard, Traveler, Ranger, Caster, plus the sword-plus-round-shield regression) made 197 Forge calls, produced baseline/equipped-idle/equipped-action/unequipped revision evidence, passed verify-artifacts and pinned Three.js inspect-glb audits on all ten equipped artifacts, passed owner and independent visual review, and matched the eight-direction attachment/validation plus the documented physically observable pixel-identity directions. Browser tests passed 2/2 at the immutable HEAD with the serialized runner. The fresh third-party K3 authoring path remains explicitly Not Assessed per owner-closure-decision.md, and the rejected sandbox reassessment harness was removed at 8f71c1d rather than weakened.
nonblocking_findings: The production bundle still emits the existing 837 KB Vite chunk-size warning.
Pixel identity evidence is limited to documented physically observable directions; attachment and validation remain eight-directional.
Armor and quiver geometry remains intentionally simplified low-poly work; the cape is a rigid extrusion without cloth physics or pose-aware drape.
Far-side equipment can be naturally self-occluded by the body.
The staff remains dark on a dark sprite background.
Skeletal deformation, inverse kinematics, cloth/equipment physics, gameplay inventory/combat state, arbitrary mesh fitting, and Unity/Godot runtime import remain out of scope of S4.
Fresh third-party K3 authoring remains Not Assessed on this host; a future successful run may add evidence in a separately approved track.
A future evidence-retention or Git LFS policy would reduce growth from repeated PNG, GLB, and transcript runs.
